name: Schnecke
prior: Madrona Labs Kaivo: 'eight different types of tuned resonators, including strings, chimes and springs' under a granular exciter, desktop, 'high CPU use' (VS: kvraudio.com/product/8429/review; synthtopia.com/?p=55518; R: musicians.md 2.6) = a spring resonator you can play, not mobile. Mutable Instruments Rings: 'string with non-linearity/dispersion (comb filter with multimode filter and non-linearities in the loop)', 'all-pass filters in the delay loop, shifting the position of the partials, which can imitate piano-string tension or more unusual inharmonic timbres', STRUCTURE = inharmonicity (VS: pichenettes.github.io/mutable-instruments-documentation/modules/rings/manual) = the dispersive Karplus loop with dispersion on a knob is Eurorack mainstream (and in VCV as Audible Instruments Resonator, A). Knas Ekdahl Moisturizer: spring reverb with exposed springs 'you can strike, bow, or otherwise manipulate by hand' plus filter, USD 425 (VS: synthtopia.com/?p=14583 'A Spring Reverb You Can Whack On'; analoguehaven.com/knas/the-ekdahl-moisturizer; signalsounds.com) = hardware, untuned. Vaelimaeki/Parker/Abel 'Parametric Spring Reverberation Effect', JAES 58(7/8) 2010: 'spectral delay filter placed into a feedback loop with a long delay line', low-frequency chirp from 'a cascade of roughly 100 interpolated stretched allpass filters', delay modulated by correlated noise; Parker 2011 EURASIP cuts the cost to one third with multirate/multiband (VS: aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=15511; acris.aalto.fi 646134; Vaelimaeki slides 2013) = effect, no pitch. u-he Twangstroem 'physically modelled springs', 'shake the virtual springs' (VS: gearnews.com), Eventide Spring, Arturia Rev SPRING-636 (VS) = effects. DAFx08 'Dispersion Modulation using Allpass Filters' (VS: dafx.de/paper-archive/2008/papers/dafx08_36.pdf). Not found: a note-tuned spring under a finger with chirp direction as Hoehe. But the physics below shows that a loop tuned to a note cannot carry an audible chirp, so the unfound thing is unfound for a reason; what is buildable is Rings' inharmonic string with a spring tank behind it.
costNotes: Measured here (M: ideas/check/sim/perf_snk_cost.js, Node 22 x64, worklet style: allpass states in locals, tanh table, lerp delay, 1-pole): M=8 loop 41.5 ns/sample = 0.199 % core = 0.34 Nebel (DSP only); M=16 60.8 ns = 0.50; two loops (L3) 88 ns = 0.73. Plus per-voice node 0.06 and 3 k-rate params 0.09 (R: webaudio.md section 4) = 0.49, plus the optional Koerper (2 native biquads 0.12) = 0.6 at L1; L3 two loops + Koerper = 1.0. Idea said 0.47 / 0.8: 25 % optimistic. The first naive loop (typed-array state, Math.tanh) cost 90 ns = 0.74 units and M=32 deoptimised to 1962 ns (M: perf_snk_sim.js) - the processor must keep the 8/16 states in locals and unroll. N fallback: a DelayNode cycle is clamped to >= 128 frames (R: webaudio.md section 7), so a live native loop is sample-exact only <= 375 Hz and frequency-quantised above; the honest fallback is the Saite pattern (offline render in the DSP worker, LRU cache, playbackRate within +-1 octave) at ~0.35 units - which could even be the primary path for a struck engine, since there the worker can afford M=100 stretched allpasses for real chirps.
soundHeld: Simulated (M: perf_snk_sim.js). (1) The tuning formula uses the group delay; the loop resonates by phase delay: with D from the group delay the fundamental is -16 ct at 220 Hz and -117 ct at 440 Hz (a=-0.85, M=8); with the phase delay -phi(w)/w it is exact, and the 1-pole LP adds another ~0.5-1 sample that must be compensated (time domain: +17/-14 ct at 220/440). (2) The partial structure depends on the note, not on the finger: a=-0.85, M=8 gives 1 : 2.00 : 3.01 : 4.03 at 110 Hz (a plain string), 1 : 2.03 : 3.11 : 4.26 : 5.49 at 220 Hz (stiff bar), 1 : 2.23 : 4.08 : 7.18 at 440 Hz (sparse bell) and no tuning at all above 498 Hz (D < 2); with M=16 the ceiling is 243 Hz, with a=-0.6, M=8 1457 Hz. The spec's 'a shrinks for high notes' therefore turns the top octave into a Saite. (3) The chirp is not there: the group-delay spread 100 Hz-5 kHz is 1.9 ms at M=8, 3.8 ms at M=16, 24 ms at M=100; an audible chirp needs >= 10-20 ms per echo (A), i.e. M = 50-100 at 2-4 units, or stretched allpasses z^-K (K=4-8 gives 7-12 ms at M=8 for the same cost) - but then the group delay at DC is 395-789 samples (8-16 ms), longer than the period of every note above 60-120 Hz, so a loop tuned to a note cannot contain the chirp: 'tuned to the note' and 'zirpendes Echo' exclude each other above ~60 Hz. (4) 'drall' (sign of a) does nothing useful: a=+0.85 has a flat 0.08-sample group delay up to 7 kHz, so the partials are exactly 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 - the sign switches dispersion off instead of reversing the chirp. Held = struck decay (like Saite); if Hoehe bends a during the hold, D must be re-solved per block or the pitch moves with the finger. What remains at Myzel pitches is Rings' inharmonic string: distinctive against Saite (harmonic) but adjacent to Kalimba/Glocke territory, and Glocke/Schale/Gong already cover inharmonic metal.
soundBurst: As a Puls hit it behaves like Saite with a bar-like ring: a 2-8 ms noise burst into the lossy loop, decay by g (T60 formula fine), Sporenregen-compatible; gates and decayMul map 1:1. The 'Boing als Rhythmus' only appears when the loop round trip is >= 20-30 ms, i.e. notes <= 30-50 Hz, below any Myzel field (fields start around 80-110 Hz, APP buildNotes) - so the Puls hears a short 'tschik' into a stiff string, not a spring. Redesign that keeps the name honest: two nested loops - a tuned string loop (D = SR/f, ~0.15 units) feeding a fixed spring tank (round trip 25-60 ms independent of pitch, M=8 stretched allpasses K=4-8, delay modulated by correlated noise as in Vaelimaeki 2010, weak return into the string); measured parts: string 0.15 + tank 0.34 + node/params 0.15 = ~0.65 units, L3 stereo tanks ~1.1; the tank's echo rate ('Umlauf') becomes the sixth parameter and the chirp per echo is then 7-12 ms at every note.
failureModes: A loop tuned to the note cannot carry an audible chirp (chirp length must stay below the period): at 80-1000 Hz the engine is a stiff/dispersive string (Rings territory), the 'Federhall' promise holds only below ~60 Hz
Tuning formula uses group delay; the loop follows phase delay: -16 ct at 220 Hz, -117 ct at 440 Hz (M); plus uncompensated LP phase
Timbre is a function of pitch, not of the finger: harmonic at 110 Hz, bar at 220, sparse bell at 440, untunable above 498 Hz (M=8, a=-0.85) or 243 Hz (M=16)
'drall' sign is a no-op: a > 0 gives flat group delay below 7 kHz (exact harmonics), it cannot flip the chirp direction with first-order sections
Cost 25 % above the estimate (0.6 / 1.0 instead of 0.47 / 0.8); typed-array state or M >= 32 in the per-sample loop deoptimises to 10-50 units
Native fallback as a live DelayNode loop is only sample-exact <= 375 Hz; use the Saite offline-render pattern instead
Hoehe during the hold changes D (D depends on a): re-solve per block or the pitch bends with the finger
verdict: Rare, not new: Kaivo has playable spring resonators (desktop), Rings puts allpass dispersion in the string loop under one knob, the Ekdahl Moisturizer lets you hit real springs, and the Vaelimaeki/Parker spring models are effects; a note-tuned spring under a finger is unfound because the physics forbids it - a loop tuned to the note cannot hold a chirp longer than its period, so above ~60 Hz the engine is a stiff inharmonic string, and the measured partials show the timbre is set by the note (string at 110 Hz, bell at 440, untunable above 498 Hz at M=8) rather than by the finger. Worklet-feasible at ~0.6 units (L3 ~1.0; 25 % over the estimate) once the tuning uses phase delay instead of group delay (the given formula is 117 ct flat at 440 Hz) and 'drall' is dropped (a > 0 simply removes the dispersion). Keep it only as the redesigned 'Saite in einem Federtank': tuned string loop feeding a pitch-independent 25-60 ms spring tank with stretched allpasses (~0.65 units), which gives the boing and the 7-12 ms chirps at every note and makes Schnecke genuinely unlike Saite, Glocke and Rings.
